answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it trades. New identities start on a narrow ridge: tiny limits, slow reputation growth. Limits widen only after repeated, attested deliveries, so a thousand fable identities buy nothing — each starts at zero, earning trust one job at a time. An identity that cheats forfeits its stake and history, so fraud costs real money. No ivory-tower faith in names: bonded stake makes trust expensive to fake and cheap to verify, because the ledger proves who did the work.
